A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ViiNeuS research work. All 17 pages, including supplementary text, equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison. Text and visual checks identify only an updated first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v4 reports original reconstruction experiments on four driving datasets, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–3, and supplementary evaluations, ablations and failure cases.

after.justification: v5 retains the same original quantitative and qualitative experiments, including the supplementary evaluations, ablations and failure cases.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical hybrid density/SDF architecture, progressive initialization, probability-based sample attribution, gradient normalization and optimization losses.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same static-scene reconstruction task on the same KITTI-360, Pandaset, Waymo and nuScenes sequences. Supplementary test scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains StreetSurf, COLMAP, OpenMVS and GOF with sparse and dense initialization. Supplementary Section 8 retains the same Neuralangelo comparisons.

E3.justification: Training budgets, sequence selection, camera/image sampling, preprocessing, baseline configurations and evaluation procedures are identical. Both retain point-to-mesh distance and precision at the 0.15 m threshold.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 and the supplementary material retain the same convergence, hybrid-stage duration, component and sample-attribution ablations, Neuralangelo investigations, and failure-case analyses.

E5.justification: Section 10.1 and Figure 7 identically report mean cumulative error curves and standard deviations across four sequences per dataset. Run-count, seed and other statistical disclosures are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match, including Tables 1–3 and the supplementary result figures. Table 2 still reports 20-minute ViiNeuS training versus 40-minute StreetSurf training.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, the rendering and SDF definitions, and the mathematical reasoning about gradient normalization in supplementary Section 7 are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning progressive SDF initialization, reconstruction across four driving datasets and approximately halved training time.

C2.justification: The explanations of density-field convergence and StreetSurf's topology dependence are unchanged. Sections 5 and 12 retain the same limitations involving thin structures near the sky, wide scenes and inaccurate monocular normals.

D1.justification: Sections 4.1 and 9 retain identical implementation settings, hyperparameters, hash-grid parameters and sequence/frame specifications. Hardware descriptions and stated access information, including links, also match.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 50 references are identical, preserving the same positioning relative to implicit surface reconstruction, MVS, driving-scene and hybrid representation methods.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v4, 3 Jan 2025 to v5, 3 Mar 2025. The prose, terminology, headings and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: All 13 figures and five tables retain identical content, captions, styling and placement. Page layout is unchanged; the updated margin-stamp text creates no layout revision.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information and presentation are identical throughout the main paper and supplementary material. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
